consisting of the ocean, the command, and the threefold divisions— then become fivefold.
Māyā is the bliss-bringer of the bhaga, the mudrā that illuminates the peak; she who is Ciñciṇī resides in the tree, and as Ciñciṇī, she exists through the bliss of the bhaga.
The power consisting of five times five, endowed with the five principles, has been attained by the Akulavīra; for him there is neither karma nor indeed ritual action.
The Kundalini is the pure moonlight, an action whose nature is inverted;
then, in a mere instant, the stainless arising bliss occurs.
Then, for the destruction of sins, one should take refuge in the Yoginīs;
[otherwise] there will be ignorance and folly throughout seven lifetimes.
"By the power of the command of the lineage (anvayājñā), the renunciation of desire is attained;
no worldly karma remains here for me, cut asunder by my initiation."
For those possessed of a mind, the yoga of action, adorned with mudrās and maṇḍalas,
leads to the severance of existence, especially within that lineage.
Kumārikākhaṇḍa: Thus, those who sever karma and whose bodies consist of the bliss of manifestation,
when the sixfold lineage is differentiated, then arousal arises.
It is joined with twelve verses and is sealed; of this there is no doubt.
It is the peak of the twelve seed-syllables in sequence, which effects the bursting of the seals.
Then, through divine ritual service, there is the pervasion of the Siddhadvādaśikā;
this is the bliss of the worlds of knowledge, consisting of sixfold bliss according to its divisions.
At that time, the state of *unmanībhāva* constitutes the lineage of the sacred seats (*pīṭha-anvaya*),
through the power of the path of Meru and the eight families (*kula*).
Thus, from the sound of Viṣṇu, the self is Kulavijñānabhairava;
free from effort and free from bliss, that splendor is attained.
Having first understood the attainment of the state (*bhāvaprāpti*) within the sixteenfold continuum in the tradition of the *Viparītakula*, one becomes a lion therein; of this there is no doubt.
The *siṃhaka* is the moon that shines even after being churned by means of another form;
because it gazes like a lion (*siṃhāvalokana*), that person is known as a "Lion" (*siṃha*).
In that regard, the Siddhas and others have been described as both consisting of the letters of the Nameless (Anāmā).
From the churning of their heart-lotuses, the Lion’s Command (siṃhājñā) is fully attained.
Having purified the self with the mantra of attraction, the three channels are made to possess the three qualities.
The wonder of Madana’s bliss then draws the entire world toward his very self.
The bliss of inverted action is Kaulīśa, the deity of the Kula;
that is the lineage of the Siddhas of awakening, and then comes the liberation of the yogins.
The all-pervading bliss has dissolved; it is the nectar of the stainless lotus, the space filled with eternal bliss, whose nature is the reversal of [worldly] activity.
The power of Māyā, capable of the movement of utterance, is the radiance that reaches the reality of Rudra’s command;
it consists of the pure consciousness of bliss and the three qualities, pervading the void as the supreme Śiva.
Because there is no distinction between the form and the liṅga, the form then shines forth.
In the four ages, the four [groups] and the tetrad arise in due order.
The single form [of the Goddess] manifests through many divisions, numbering in the tens of millions and beyond count.
Twenty-seven principal divisions have been proclaimed;
first among them is the group of four, which are the well-known *pīṭhas* that bestow success.
Those peaks are joined with lamps; likewise, by them occurs the first arising.
From the sky-farer situated in the midst of the sky-faring birds, there is also the sky-farer.
That is the partless supreme space, and then the Udyāna-Bhairava.
The Kumārikā section belongs to Kaumāra; its light resides in the center of Śakti at Maṇipūraka.
This is the seat (pīṭha) originating from Jālandhara, which effects the destruction of darkness.
The crest-jewel situated in the center of the moon, intensely radiant with the bliss of form,
is the bliss of the Lord of Authorities (Adhikārīśvara), known by the name Pūrṇapīṭha.
Bestowing desires, supreme bliss, and rest within the form of desire; when the flood has arisen in its own nature, then that is Kāmarūpaka.

Through the differentiation of the four principles, there is the tetrad of the four mudrās; because of their non-difference from the form and the sign, the form then shines forth. And in the four ages, the fourfold group likewise appears in succession.
In the region beyond Kāmarūpa, and also at the three river confluences.
From that very reversal of the sequence, that which is called Tisra arises;
it is situated in the center at the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra), established as the peak, consisting of the bliss of consciousness.
At the end of the Kali age, there will be another; all beings shall be dissolved into the fifth Lord of the Pīṭha.
Through the cessation of the three channels.
And that Self, by obstructing the gate of Brahman, would eternally pervade;
the Mudrās, Siddhas, and the four Pīṭhas were brought down to Candradvīpa.
The primary [deities] are in the Western Tradition (paścimāmnāya), which is unknown in other systems;
in the Kumārikākhaṇḍa,
they reside at the southern gate in Koṅkaṇa in the Southland (dakṣiṇāpatha).
The immovable seat (pīṭha) arises as the presiding authority over the five;
furthermore, there is another authority which is unchanging within the state of childhood.
"The seat known as Adhikāra was revealed by Ṣaṣṭhīśa; and that very [seat], having reached the Kali age, was made manifest by his command."
Those who are devoid of Koṅkaṇa do not achieve success through the five;
this is declared to be the sacred seat (pīṭha), and Koṅkaṇa resides within one's own body.
In Koṅkaṇa there is Koṅkaṇeśa, and from the churning [of the ocean] comes Koṅkaṇa;
situated in the Bindu and located in Candrapurī, that is the state of Koṅkaṇa.
Situated at the top of the vulva and located within the sphere, it bestows perfect accomplishment;
these two, the Moon and the Sun, reside in the three seats of Koṅkaṇa.
In the lineage of the wheel of both luminosities, there are two lamps;
the seat and the descent of the seat are endowed with the five principles.
And that place where their authority shall reside will be the supreme seat (pīṭha), Koṅkaṇa, which possesses that authority.
The six seats (pīṭhas) of the Sixfold One, according to the sequence of the six modes,
are considered the first [set] in the lineage, being joined with the external limbs.
Having reached [the mandala] in due order, those rays of external form which reside within the mandala achieve success; they should be known as the first [to be mastered].
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa:
thereafter, the others and the rest, each separately according to the division of the sequence;
having first known the six sacred seats (pīṭhas), one then becomes a member of the lineage (anvayika).
"Without knowing the fault that arises from the sixfold seat of causes, others indeed resort to the subtle; now I shall tell you that."
Within one's own body is the Great Seat (mahāpīṭha), which is a single seat of six kinds;
it is the void that takes the form of the worlds through its counter-clockwise rotation.
Like a bird, one should cause the self to wander through the Udyāna-pīṭha;
then, having emerged from that, when the self has reached the station of the Sun (Ravi),
the state of dissolution of the worlds is called the "Net" (Jāla), which is partless (niṣkala).
Through its conjunction with the abode of the wind, a digit of the moon is produced.
The joy arising from the emergence of all bliss is situated in the North and is full;
it is the bliss residing in the wind-element which is slowly generated through churning.
Having pierced through the state of Rudra-Śakti, it is the form of desire (kāmarūpaka) located in the semen.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa:
from semen arises the Nāda, whose form is the bliss of the self of Nāda.

Because it is churned by the bliss of the *bhaga* through the power of the division of the three, that which is called "the Three" is proclaimed; therefore, it reaches the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*) within one's own body.
Through the power of the other, that which pierces through space is the supreme yoga; it is the distinction between the lower and the higher.
Thereafter, a state arises established in the station of the abandonment of the five;
the cluster [of energies] has gone into the sky of the image of Koṃkaṇa.
Situated within the Kadamba-golaka, the Koṅkaṇa of Śiva is the seat of the Vijñānakula for the purpose of illuminating that which is to be known.
Residing within the self of all beings, from that the mind arises;
from the principle of mind, speech is born, and it dissolves into the bliss of the ultimate reality.
Even from the churning of the mind, when the syllable Oṃ is established in the vital breath (anila),
fire is ignited by that breath and consumes the latent impressions of the other [world].
Then, by the power of that radiance, the abode of flames from the network of the sun,
having dissolved into the mind's organ of generation, there arises the light within the moon.
Because it swallows all artistic powers (*kalā*) through churning, that which flows forth as the essence of supreme bliss— the *ānandakaulika*— is the *kāmarūpaka*.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa:
Through the power of the essence of unctuousness, it is sattvic due to the influence of the Supreme;
even by the mere remembrance of the Cakra, that which is called Tisra consists of half a measure.
The half-mora is the Supreme Power; through its threefold division, it is the power of Rudra.
It shines as the non-contraction of the Self—Koṅkaṇa, the Kuṇḍa and the Golaka.
There are six seats (pīṭhas) and six blisses (ānandas); even a single seat is sixfold through the awakening to the sixfold meaning and the investigation of the four quarters.
There are six seats (pīṭhas), the group of six Siddhas, and the six goddesses of the seats;
there are six mudrās, the sixfold [system], the six ages (yugas), and that which is designated as the group of six.

Through thirty-six divisions of six each, the reality of the seat (*pīṭhasadbhāva*), which illuminates the sixfold knowledge, has been explained according to the meaning of the stages (*bhūmikārtha*).

Thus, in the introduction to the Great Sacrifice of Manthānabhairava, in the lineage comprising seventy million verses emerged from the Path of Meru, exceeding one hundred thousand quarters, on the path of the primordial seat, in the determination of the subsequent sixfold division of the Vimalabheda, in the *Kādi* division, in the *Svāminīmata* of the Supreme Lord’s command, in the venerable compendium of twenty-four thousand verses spoken in the *Ambākrama*, [this is] the Foundation of the Seats (*pīṭhabhūmikā*).
In the description of the transformations, this is the bliss named Kramodaya.
The venerable Kaulīśa said: "If, first of all, the six seats (pīṭhas) have been purified for the sake of the stages (bhūmikās),"
And the manifestation of the sacred seats (pīṭha) exists within one's own body according to the meaning of the stages (bhūmikā).
"Now tell me, O knower of mantras, how the lineage of the seats (pīṭha) comes to be.
The venerable Vakrā said: [This is] the sixty-first bliss.
And she alone is the mistress of the seats (pīṭhas), the one who reveals the supreme state.
And she, established firmly in the state of non-duality by virtue of her non-dual nature,
has dissolved into the continuum of the six seats and arisen sequentially.
The moist, single-syllable womb is of six types; it is a mass in the form of the letter *e*, resembling the sky.
Devoid of pleasure and pain, she is the Mistress of Birds (Garuḍa) situated in the midst of the sky;
and by means of the differentiation of the syllables, she is the moonlight of the uncontracted Ākula.
Kubjikā is the deity in the garden of the seat of Kamalāmbhas;
she is Klinnā, Śāvarī, Tejovṛddhi, and Prakāśinī.
One should practice the wandering of austerity out of a desire for the splendor of others.
Through austerity, she known as Śāvarī, who expands the Siddhayoga, [arises].
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa, Cāmuṇḍā, the renowned Siddhayoginī, is the Śāvarī of the Kula.
She is the mistress of the Jālapīṭha, the presiding deity of the sacred seat.
Pervading the six seats, she is the embodiment of the self of space;
she is the divider of the Kula and Kaula of the Kulaparvatarāja.
The host of Śāvarīs is the bliss of the Residue marked by the moon;
the Yoginīs who possess a portion of Koṅkaṇa are the deities named Koṅkaṇās.
The deity of Pūrṇapīṭha is Śavarī, who belongs to Koṅkaṇa;
she resides in the midst of the filaments of the lotus, piercing through the location of Klinnā.
Through the abandonment of inhalation and exhalation, by the playful power of Śavarī,
and through the churning of the wheel, the essence of the mind-born god (Kāma) arises.
Maṅgalā, Śāvarī, and Nandā are the deities of Kāmarūpa;
she who is the deity of Kāmarūpa is that which is equal, and she is declared to be the supreme (parā).
Śavarī, who is both Samanā and Unmanā, exists in the form of pure conscious awakening;
she resides in the station of Mātaṅga and is adorned with the syllable of Madana.
She is indeed proclaimed as Madanā, and she is also the Mātaṅga-samaya;
her ascetic practice consists of the knowledge born of Śāvarī belonging to the fifth Pīṭha.
The sovereign power Śakti, who possesses authority, will appear at the end of the Kali age;
she is equal to all yoginīs, the goddess of gods, the maiden.
The Kumārikā-khaṇḍa is situated in the midst of Kośala; she is skilled in the Ciñciṇī-kula.
The deity is Koṅkaṇā, the remainder being adorned by the radiant Koṅkaṇa.
Flowing forth in the hexagon, she is the six deities of the six seats;
she has made manifest the entirety of the triangle and the mountain.
From the churning of the world of Śukra, the six deities emerged;
the six seats (pīṭhas) are their subtle forms, while the six goddesses are their gross manifestations.
Established by the Lord of Mantras, she is endowed even with the three qualities;
through the nature of the Space-Linga, she consists of six powers and has a sixfold essence.
But she, born or unborn within the circle of mothers in six ways,
is then the differentiation of one's own mantra through the subduing of one's own body.
On the seat (pīṭha), the subtle, internal activity of the authority over the seat resides; it is located in the bindu, known as Ghūrmaṇī, and indeed the Anāmā is composed of consciousness.
In the supreme space of the principle of intellect (buddhitattva), Kubjikā is the deity Rudra;
in the supreme space of the clockwise whorl, she is the purification of the lower sun. Taking up the station of obstruction, Śavarī is the deity of knowledge.
The primordial power, self-existent, is the pervasion of the radiance of the knowledge of Rudra.
Koṃkaṇā is the deity Vāmadeva;
situated in the center of the full moon,
that digit of Śaṅkara shines forth through the union of the left and the right.
In the form of the bliss of emergence, she is named Maṅgalā;
from the renunciation of the fourfold fame, there are the syllables of the four morae.
The power of Maṅgī possesses the capacity for contrary action; through its threefold nature, this Kuṇḍalinī power is impelled by Udāna and arises from the letter Ya.
Through the union with the letter of the nameless (Anāmikā), Koṅkaṇā is in the house of Koṅkaṇa;
by the power of the divine Śaktis, there are six seats (pīṭhas) in the six houses.

This teaching of the Divine Current (divyaugha), which instructs in the reasoning for the unity of all things internal and external, consists of the sixfold Kula of the Current of the Seats (pīṭhaugha).
Having recognized the mouth of the Guru as the Supreme Power (Parāśakti), one should worship the sacred seats (pīṭhas);
among them, the lineage of the Siddhas (siddhaugha) is the other [lower power], which possesses a sixfold authority of its own.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa,
having understood the pervasion of the light of primordial gnosis (ughajñāna), one becomes part of the lineage of the Siddhas;
[therein resides] Kaulīśa, the stainless sky, situated on the shore of the glorious ocean.
And that great Siddha Coḍḍīśa is the master of his own authority over the Bhagas;
this is indeed the awakening of the Fire of the Kulaparvatarāja.
The Khamantra, the practice of gnosis, and Caryābhairava in that which is called Jāla—
[he is] situated in the midst of full-blown bliss, born from the seat of the youthful dawn.
O Ānanda, one should contemplate the sixth Bhairava, held by the Moon, abiding in the Full,
situated in the midst of the series of worlds, and encapsulated by Māyā.
By the power of the Goddess’s command, [he attained] Avasthānandabhairava;
situated in the midst of the ocean and mountains, he was surrounded by great wisdom.
Mātaṅgī, intoxicated by passion, is the imperishable power; situated within stainless knowledge, Koṅkaṇa is of the nature of action. (From the Kumārikākhaṇḍa)
From the support of the mind also arises the stainless power Koṅkaṇā;
the six Siddhas, the six Pīṭhas, the Goddesses of the Pīṭhas, and the Bhairavas— all of whom,
by the grace of Bhairava’s command, consist of a single arising in one place.
This is the investigation of the lineage of the Siddhas, the arising of the sequence of the knowledge of the Ogha.
O Lord Ciñciṇīnātha, through the application of the sixfold meaning, [the syllable] is sixfold:

situated in the middle of space, it is the single letter *kha*, the triple *kha*, and the supreme and non-supreme *kha*; O Lord Uḍīśa, who delights in consciousness, it is filled with space by means of the wind.
With the letter *kṣa* as the preceding syllable, it completes the three-measure phrase.
The pervasion of the nectar of the space of conduct; conduct is the consciousness of Ciñciṇī, which strikes the belly of the jar of the vital breath above, below, and in the middle.

The Ghaṇṭikā mountain is the sixth, which causes the heart-lotus to blossom. Between nectar and death, whatever conceptualization of friend and foe arises for one whose mind is exhausted of discursive thought, that is called "attainment" (siddhi), born of passion.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa,
within the village of Mattamātaṅga, Madana is the portion of life.
That pervasion which occurs through the differentiation of the collection of phonemes resides within the limbs of that intoxication;
from the reverse order comes stainless bliss, the fire situated in the lotus.
The yogi, devoted to the six locations, [attains] the nectar of his own office, which is the stainless peak-syllable situated within the dissolved six-footed one.
Those whose selves are filled with the six yogas, within the seats of the lineage of the six Siddhas,
have accomplished the practice of the Siddhakrama for both Siṃhaka and Siṃhikā.
Then, from the churning of the wheel, there arises the sixfold knowledge;
the sixfold means of action, and the sixfold determination of the Kula.
The sixfold application of meaning constitutes the six seats (ṣaṭpīṭha);
it is the agency of the Supreme Self in the performance of conduct and the exercise of its creative power.
The self that has gone outside to external existence, and that very self which is sixfold—
the supreme shadow consists of six groups of six, and the supreme digit consists of six groups of six.
Vimala: Kamala is infinite;
Kamala is infinite; he is the gatherer of the nectar of Kamalā.
The sixfold [mantra] is "sarvopa aiṃkāram."
One who knows the expansion of perfected bliss, the earring of the elements of the world,
the *kuṇḍalinī*, the skull, the cessation, and the skull [itself].
Vibhāvānanda-Kailāsa, Upadeśaka-Kailāsa,
Kūṭāntastha-Kailāsa, and [Svabhāva-]Kailāsa— these are the four divisions in sequence.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa:
The triple wheel situated within the wheel of the three measures and the bindu is both supreme (parā) and non-supreme (aparā).
Since no defect exists therein, O Siddhabhairava, it is the seat of the sacred seats (pīṭhas).
And then there is another, the supreme pervader, the highest Śiva;
then the flood of the moon's rising is established within the self of the sun.
Moonlight is produced by the descent of the moon and sun; for even though the moon is the agent of the act of producing light, it acts as an instrument toward its own effect.
Then, through the awakening of sensory cognition, there is the instruction of Śambhu;
thus are the rays that form the enclosure of the city of Candrapura.
The city of the Moon (Candrapuryaka) consists of the ornament of the ruby of expanding gnosis;
it is that very primordial bliss, the letter *e*. Within the self of creative ideation (*kalana*), the letters *ha* and *kṣa* are the supreme luster that nourishes even the entire world.
O best of gods, the letter *A* is a certain crescent digit of the Supreme Lord;
by it, O life-force, one flourishes in Koṅkaṇa and Kāmarūpa.
It is the life-force of the lineage of Śiva.
Due to the differentiation of the three trees, a person attains what is called the individual soul (jīva);
thus does the supreme power (parā-śakti) exist as the individual soul within the pentad of prāṇa, apāna, and the rest.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa,
the station of the *samāna* arises from both *prāṇa* and *apāna*;
by means of the *samāna*, one attains the *kaulikī* accomplishment of the Moon.
The supreme space remains perfectly tranquil as the teacher;
it consists of the letter Ū, the letter U, and the letter Ca as the third.
The moonlight of the crescent digit is the supreme Śiva unified as one;
the letter *u* is like *ra*, and *ṛ*, *ṝ*, and *r* are within *ṝ*.
The letter *ḷ*, the letter *lū*, and the letter *ha* at the end are imperishable; the vowel sound *ū* is joined together with the two *u*s.
Known as the sound that causes the moon to open, it is colored by the vowel *a* and enclosed within the two cavities of the breasts in the form of the syllable *ā*.
Having made the non-vessel (apuṭa) into a vessel (puṭa), both the rising and the setting [of the breath] are unified into a single vessel; this is known by the designation "Kalpa.
*Rā*, *ri*, *ari*, *rānanda*, and the syllable *rā*—thus the letter *ra* is sixfold.
Then, there is the bliss arising from the power (śakti), known as Vaiṣṇava, which is threefold.
Impelled by the power of consciousness (cic-chakti), the Haṃsa [reveals] the Kula lineage within the belly of the Haṃsa;
that Kula extends to the end of the Kaula-kalā, for the Timeless One (vikāla) is of the nature of creative pulsation (kalanā).
From the reckoning [of time] comes Kālikā, Kālī, and Kālakaṅkālakaulikī;
she arises within the Kula as Time, yet is undisturbed and free from time.
Kaulīśa is situated in the midst of Kula; Kaulīśa is the designator of Kula.
When the Skull is joined with the Kalās, then the Kalā is the Face of the Crow (Kākīmukhā).
Seated upon the Lion of the Kālikā-kula, he is adorned by the power (śakti) of Kālikā.
The manual for the sequence of Kālikā is presented according to the distinction between those who have accomplished their task and those who have not.
Contraction and expansion, as well as the radiance of the Supreme Self—
the physical orb is that which has emerged from the light consisting of the surging consciousness.
The Kumārikākhaṇḍa is the form of the crow (KĀ), the letter MA, and the manifold display of the syllable KU;
it is the manifestation of Gaṇeśa, the sky, and the sovereign letter HA.
ĀṬA and MAṬAHA indeed rule over that which is without beginning;
the letter ṬA is situated within the space of existence, between the letters CA and THA.
Then that Śāvarī-Śakti, who has the moon as her crest-jewel,
is the illuminator Mahākālī in the form of pure Great Consciousness;
she is the emergence, the cauldron, and the center of the haṭa within the two pathways.
Kaṭaha-vikhyātopa is the cessation; Koṅkaṇa is the abode.
Āḍharūpaka, māṭaṃ, paṭala, and paṭalāmṛta;
herein, of the wave of nectar (amṛtataraṅga), ahicchatra is the supreme nectar (parāmṛta).
The Lord who is the source of the descent, the Lord who is the measure of both, the root of the desire to create and destroy, the immortal one, and the city of the moon.

The Moon and the lunar light are the supreme shadow; the Moon and the one whose crest is the half-moon are the Nāda known by the name Śilāśekhara. The remaining digits of the Sun and Moon constitute the mandala of the sixteen vowels.
The supreme seventeenth digit has ascended to the stainless state.
From the abandonment of truth comes the seventh station; rest is the eighth, and dissolution is the abode.
The supreme bliss is the *ālaya*; the letter *A* is the essence of the consciousness of Śiva.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa:
Then, through the destruction of time, Śakti is Amāvāsyā and likewise Ambikā; by the cessation of the station of the Haṃsa, she is the supreme digit (kalā) known as Haṃsa.
The deity named Haṃsinī resides in the middle of the "haṃsa" and other [mantras];
through the division of the higher and the lower, she awakens one to the auspicious state (śiva) of the words.
The vital breath (prāṇa) resides within Meru; the moon resides within the vital breath;
and the sun resides within the moon, situated between the power of Meru and the emission (visarga).
The emission situated between two emissions is of the nature of arising;
it is the emission established in the One, existing within both the one and the many emissions.
That which is called Nāda, transcending the Visarga, assuming the form of the state of Nināda, consisting of three steps and pervading the six steps— then it vibrates within Koṅkaṇa.
Koṅkaṇa resides within the lotus, yet Koṅkaṇa is even more subtle than the lotus;
Koṅkaṇa is called Nāda through the moon, and the auspicious Koṅkaṇa is that which is named Nāda.
In the center of Śiva is the Bindu; in the center of the Bindu is that which is Śiva. That which is at the end of Nāda resides in the center of Śiva, and at its end is the splendor of Śiva.
At the end of that splendor is the bliss of Śiva; Śiva is subtle and sixfold.
Śiva is endowed with sixfold power; Śiva and Śakti are both the higher and the lower.
In the supreme-non-supreme supreme space, [resides] the sequence of the supreme-non-supreme steps;

the bird, filled with the supreme beyond both sequence and non-sequence, moves within the power of breath. In the *Kumārikākhaṇḍa*, situated in the midst of power, it is silent; in the midst of silence is the *kadambaka* cluster.
At the end of the Kadamba is the Bilva; at the end of the Bilva is the Cittaciñciṇī.
Ciñciṇī is the supreme Śakti, residing in the Bhaga within the self of the Bhaga.
O Mahimānanda, you who abide within, [this is] the Mahimā-jñāna in the Kulakrama.
Mahimā is the supreme power (*parā śakti*); Mahimā is also Anāmikā.
She is Mananā and Manādyā; she is Anantā, that Anāmikā who is contained within Anāmā.
She is Jyeṣṭhā, and she arises from the differentiated *kalā*.
The knower and creator of his own position, the distinguisher between what is his own side and what is not.
Śiva is the bliss of the indivisible and the divider, the illuminator of the Haṃsa;
having known the fivefold flood, this is remembered as the Lion Gesture (siṃhaka) convention.
Even by performing the syllable *aiṃ* while the *siṃhaka* is situated in reverse order,
from that inversion arises the auspicious state that is free of waves.
In the lineage succession.
Having extracted the sequence of words, the utterance of the words,
the nectar, the lord, the digit, the principle,
and the word that concludes all;
But within the flood of words, phrases, and syllables, there are the words, phrases, and syllables themselves.
O Great Lord, you possess the supreme equanimity of discernment and the state of a lion.

One should enter that supreme state by means of the cessation of the perishable and the imperishable, having fully contemplated the grasping of the self; then I abide within the body, which is blissless and incomparable.
Then one should perform the triple bliss; the movement is three-syllabled and follows the three paths.
Blocked by the threefold movement, the coming and going occurs in space.
Having reflected upon the coming and going that consists of the image and its adjuncts—
the eternal bliss, the supreme bliss, the bliss whose nature is Bhairava— [one should contemplate it].
The three-syllabled [mantra] transcends the three paths; the three-syllabled [mantra] has arrived in a threefold way.
It is the perishable essence of all without exception, the confluence of the syllables of the *śṛṅgāṭaka*.
On Kailāsa, at the peak of Meru, is Meruśṛṅgāṭabhairava;
in the Manthānabhairava sacrifice, there is the lineage of seventy million verses.
In the non-divine, human world, [it is] the instruction on the ground of the Siddhas;

thus begins the descent in the great sacrifice of Mahāmanthānabhairava, in the lineage measuring seventy million verses, emerged from the path of Meru, exceeding one hundred thousand quarters, descending upon the primordial seat, the Seat of Knowledge (Vidyāpīṭha), in the Vimalabheda-Uttaraṣaṭka.

In the *Nirṇaya*, within the division beginning with *Ka*, in the *Ājñāpārameśvara* according to the *Svāminīmata*, in the venerable compendium of twenty-four thousand verses spoken in the tradition of the Mother (*Ambākrama*), in the description of the chapter on the stages of the Siddha Goddess,
this is the bliss named the Arising of the Sequence (*Kramodaya*). The venerable Kaulīśa said:

And for the sake of the stages (*bhūmikā*) of the goddesses and the perfected ones (*siddha*), I have heard [the teaching] regarding the five jewels and the sixfold [set], as well as the fivefold and threefold stages.
"Out of compassion, speak, O knower of mantras! How may the ocean of knowledge be attained?
Śrīvakrā said:
[This is] the sixty-second bliss.
The pervasion of the qualities of the five faculties is the activity of the arising of the five jewels.
In brief, the five jewels within the five [deities] of Kriyāyoga are Brahmā,
Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva.
And when these five, endowed with the application of the *kalās* and possessed of the five jewels, are brought together in one place, then one becomes long-lived and brings about auspiciousness.
Through the application of the five mudrās, the five jewels are the cause;
a single jewel situated in the midst of the jewels, enclosed within the womb of the jewels.
Having attained the jewel of the *ratlikā*, the mind becomes like a jewel;
when the mind and the jewel are in a state of equal unity, one possesses a stable nature and intelligence.

Then the functioning of the object of knowledge arises according to the tradition taught by Ratnā; the object of knowledge is situated within knowledge, and its pervasion resides within the object of knowledge. (Kumārikākhaṇḍa)
Then, by means of the *palitanirṇā*, it arises in a single eon;
thus, through the yoga of the oral tradition, one should practice the five jewels.
For one whose mind is exhausted of conceptual construction, the elixir is accomplished;
yet when the delusion of conceptual construction is destroyed, you remain established in non-conceptuality.
Having brought about the destruction of conceptual construction, then success is attained without a doubt;
the lunar yoga is the entire self, the primordial nature, the cage of one's own self.
Through the cessation of the three qualities (guṇas), the state is seen like the moon;
when the movement of the moon has ceased, one should abandon the lunar sign and the solar sign.
Furthermore, through the emission of the two seed-syllables (śukra), the supreme pervasion of the Supreme Reality is proclaimed, wherein the lower reality is cast aside.
In the supreme space is the supreme bindu, the pentad of the five jewels;
situated within the womb of that lotus of power is the tree of the three families (trikula).
Having known the family tree of the goddesses, a man becomes accomplished;
Bhairava resides within the womb of Śakti as the Triple Family (trikula) arisen from the six wheels.
It should abide like the space of the sky; the sky is like the sky. O Gaganānanda, the letter Ga is the supreme nectar situated in the sky.
Accompanied by the emission (*visarga*) and situated within the emission, it possesses the authority of the Mother Samanā;
it is the power that is both supreme and non-supreme, the imperishable syllable upon the petals of the lotus— this is the *Kumārikākhaṇḍa*.
The syllable called *pa* has the form of wind;
the syllable *ma* extends to the end of time, and the syllable *ma* is the embodiment of power (*śakti*).
When all the jewels are filled, there is the fourth letter, *ma*.
Standing in the midst of the space of *ma*, it is itself the form of the Mother.
Joined with the *kalās*, it is called by the name *na*; it is certainly called by the name *na*.
At the end of the jewel of the breath-exhalation, it dissolves into the supreme state.
Due to the differentiation of the five steps, the living being reaches the knot of Brahman; having entered the supreme abode by means of power, it consists of the manifestation of power.
The exhaustion of the activity of the organs of action occurs at that very moment. The Kumārikākhaṇḍa consists of the Ṣaṭaka,
the Paṭaha, the Sāṭaka, and likewise the Paṭala.
Having understood the union of both, one then becomes long-lived;
possessing a lotus-like vessel of blood, one becomes a mountain of stainless knowledge.
Having known the family tree of the goddesses, one will become accomplished;
[the names are] Nara, Nāra, Nagā, Ekā, Nara, and likewise Nārāntaka.
Having understood the state of human existence, there is then the consecration of that state;
and through the sprinkling of the consecration, the *piṇḍa* is stirred at that very moment.
Through the consecration from the ocean of stainless bliss in space,
he is then liberated as a sky-clad one by means of the yoga of the bliss of manifestation.
Even from the supporting of the stainless jewel, there is no differentiation;
as long as the state arises, that is gnosis, the fivefold jewel.
For one whose mind has been rendered free of desire by the water that effects cessation,
having understood the instruction on the jewel, the command of the jewel is certainly accomplished.
O Kaulīśa, the single jewel situated in the midst of jewels, enclosed within the cavity of the interior of jewels, is the syllable-jewel; O Lord of the Kula, it is the fivefold jewel.
Thus, I have first proclaimed to you this glorious *pañcaratna-rasāyana*, beginning with the *avatāra* extracted from the City of the Moon (*candrapura*).
The supreme bliss within the womb of the jewel, the very expansion of consciousness,
enriched with the artistry of the jewel of the mind— this is the one jewel, both transcendent and immanent.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa:
The great jewel situated within the cave exists as one in sixteen ways;
because of its division into sixteen syllables, the syllable *aiṃ* is the imperishable jewel.
One should abide with sixteen [syllables], including the differentiation of existence (*bhavabheda*) and the mind-transcending (*manottara*),
as well as the ocean of the womb (*yonyārṇava*) adorned with the syllable *aiṃ* and the letter *ī*.
In the Kali age, they remain together with Kumuda and Sutejas;
the four jewels—A, Ā, I, and Ī—are situated at the front in Kāmarūpaka.
The vowels u, ū, ṛ, and ṝ reside in the jewels; they are situated on the right and manifest as a web-like form.
Arisen in the Tretā Yuga, they are the ornaments of Dakṣa and Kumāra.
Lṛ, lū, e, and ai—these four jewels are situated on the left as the deities of the Full Moon;
having reached the Dvāpara Yuga, they are elevated by the command of the Crown.
Oṃ, au, aṃ, aḥ—these four jewels, situated in the center, shine as the syllables in the Kṛta Yuga within the abode of Uḍḍīyāna; they are the self-luminous command of the Sky-farer.
Thus, the sixteen jewels and the sixteen digits-jewels have been described in sequence; all these are the five principal jewels.
The letter *a*, the letter *i*, *e*, *ai*, and *aḥ* as the fifth— these, in the arising of the jewels, are the illuminators of the five jewels.
"These twenty-five, descended from the lineage of Candrapurya, have been extracted through ten divisions; by knowing this, one attains the supreme state."
Sāṭaka, Paṭaka, Sāvaka, Paṭaha, Ṭaṭaha, Paṭahānanda—this is the instruction on the five jewels. In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa:
the jewel is situated in the middle of the serpent, and the sun is situated in the middle of the jewel.
At that time, there was indeed one renowned as Ratneśvara in the Vakrikā doctrine.
From the *kumbha* [to] the *kumbha* beyond the *kumbha*, within the syllables beginning with the *kumbha* of the Sun,
the fivefold pervasion proceeds by dividing the digits (*kalā*) of the initial groups of consonants.
The state of the three qualities is the veil; the activity consists of the nature of vital breath (prāṇa).
It is characterized by the authority of Ratnanātha, whose consciousness is the bliss of creative contemplation (bhāvanā).
Of the non-jewel, the jewel, and the two jewels, there is the jewel-like person;
O Ānanda, the jewel-treasure stands at the end of the persons.
The jeweled handle of this jewel,
by means of the application of jewels and gems, is declared to be the "jewel-union" (*ratnayoga*).
But for a variegated jewel,
that which illuminates the precious gem is indeed the gold, even though it appears in a reversed order.
It is gold among metals, the gold of gold, and the seed of Brahman;
through the piercing of the channel of Brahman, it is the instructor of the life-force of Brahman.
This is the instruction for liberation and the sphere of the passionless;
it is the ever-arisen piercing of Brahman by one purified as a portion of Brahman, which shines with ever-arisen consciousness as the practice of "unmattabrahmacarya" (the ecstatic celibacy).
And celibacy—this fivefold vow is stainless.
Thus, the Brahma-syllable space is joined with the Self in five ways as "space"; it is the illuminator of the fivefold Self. [From] the Kumārikākhaṇḍa.
Having divided space fivefold and having divided the void fivefold, one unifies the fivefold knowledge; this is the teaching of the five times five.
The power consists of five fives; the activity consists of five fives;
there is the pervasion of the five-fifths of the kalās, and one should utter the five jewels.
Fivefold:
when the jewel resides in emission (visarga), it is the five jewels residing in the fourth state.
Through union with the five mudrās, the path is the five jewels.
The illuminator.
The three channels and the three jewels should be purified; one channel is preeminent.
Having made the city both pure and impure, purification then arises.
The vow is threefold; the power of the vow belongs to one whose mind has become Śiva. Having attained a firm bodily state through that Śiva-like detachment, she indeed then [attains liberation].
The body;
that which pertains to the holy life.
And having attained oneness,
this becomes the movement of the signs for one whose mind has been pierced by the Sugata.
Thus is the instruction on the jewels; where the five jewels reside, such is the instruction on the five [jewels] in the tree and in the western house.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa,
the tree-form of the Lord of the Western House is within the womb of the *bhaga*;
and where the five jewels reside is within the womb of that *bhaga*.
The bliss existing within the trees is called the Jewel Tree;
this very [tree] of the five jewels is situated upon Mount Kailāsa.
Thus, the well-known flood of mantra-arising is the five jewels;
through its various divisions, one and many, that lineage is the five jewels.
The sign of the lineage (gotra-liṅga) exists in sixteen divisions according to its forms;
through the differentiation of the five jewels, the lineage follows the sequence of the Amarikās.
At the end of the sequence, by the will of Śiva, the five jewels situated in the middle of the sequence [are attained];
that is the summary of the practice through the application of the supreme space (parākāśa).
O Bhairava, the foundation of one's own family is the foundation;
that family consists of twenty-five principles and is of five kinds.
Having performed the sixfold investigation of the Jewel of the Kula belonging to the Lord of Kula, according to the sequence of the path of Kula, that then becomes the instruction on gnosis.
Knowledge is said to have a firm objective, and knowledge itself has a firm characteristic;
knowledge, by its very nature as reality, abides in the midst of the objective and its characteristics.
The wise one, through the single cause, [perceives] the mind situated within silence;
then it attains that Nirvāṇa which is the Kaulika bliss of dissolution. In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa, the lotus-shaped sphere resides within the center of Kaulīśa.
And that indeed is the Kaulika-bliss; it is proclaimed as being endowed with all parts.
Having merged the differentiated into the undifferentiated, and the undifferentiated into the essence of the differentiated,
then Yoga proceeds, which teaches peaceful knowledge.
Khaparaika and khaparaika;
kapāṭa is the same as kapāṭasya, while kharpara is its [synonym].
The supreme state:
when the moon arises from the letter *kha* of the skull-bowl (*kharpara*), then that form of Śambhu is attained as an object to be grasped through meditative absorption.
The letter *ma* belongs to the letter *kha*, and the letter *sa* belongs to the letter *ma*;
thus, the pervasion at the end is made manifest.
In the letter *ha* at the end of a word ending in *sa*, and in the two *visargas* at the end of a word ending in *ha*.
This vessel of the five jewels, endowed with thirty-eight digits and complete with the five mudrās, is declared to be the Moon-vessel (śaśipātra).
For one whose mind has reached fullness in its course, one should apply the letter *ma*;
having formed the city of the half-moon, one will then achieve heroic accomplishment (*vīrasiddhi*).
"O jewel among heroes and lords of yogins, [this teaching] is more precious than even a mine of jewels;
it stands in the midst of the syllable *ṭa*,
illuminating the hero’s trident."
Having made the seventeenth digit of this very mass of jewels marked with the plane of innate vitality (sahajauja), one should sever the hero’s fetters.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa,
the letter *kha* and the letter *pha*, augmented by the radiance of the letter *ra*,
are joined with the five seats (*pañcapīṭha*) and conjoined with fire and poison.
She is declared to be the Scissors for the threefold bond;
she is the purifying deity Kālī, who pierces the vital points and brings an end to the city [of the body].
The lotus of Kartariśa is the abode of nectar for poison;
having first purified it through practice, one may then consume that which was previously inedible.
One who is freed from states that have completely dissolved is both liberated and not liberated; of this there is no doubt.
Having made the mind free of doubt, one should then point out the cause:
through the abandonment of six, liberation occurs in the seventh; through the abandonment of five, the mind is conquered.
Having known Raudrī in the abode of those who are eternally united, one shall attain the state.
The supreme practice regarding the entire ocean is the immortal state;
by relinquishing all dualities, a person attains the Heart.
Karavīra, Karavīra, Karavīrakara,
as well as Vikarāla, Karāla, Karālī, and furthermore Kartarī.
The Udayasaṃpradāya consists of the Saṃvarta and Kartarī-kara;
the Merumālā consists of the Kapāla and the Kartarī-yuta.
In the state of being the agent, knowledge is the instrument due to the connection between cause and effect;
at that time, she is the supreme power, Saṃvartakaravīrakā.
When the *kaulikī* arises for the inverted tree,
then there is the mutual union of both and of the jewels.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa:
The mind of one another is Māyā, and it perceives coming and going;
it is both supreme and non-supreme, distinguished as supreme-non-supreme and supreme.
Thus, there is mutual knowledge of both the rising and the setting; his form moves through the great space, possessing both supreme and non-supreme forms.
Then the probe of knowledge consists of both the formless and the formed in succession;
indeed, the formless, the formed, and the fivefold-formed belong to the wind.
The formless is the supreme reality; the formless is the fifth state (*pada*).
Through the churning of the oneness of the five cities of form, rays [of light] emerge.
And the attainment of qualities proceeds like [the emergence of jewels] from the churning of the ocean;
the mantra, the superior mudrā, and the *karṇikā* which is the mantra-mudrā.
And Vikarālā is called the Mudrā; the practice consists of churning, the knowledge of the reverse movement, and the reverse lion-posture.
Therein is another knowledge consisting of twelve verses, which reverses names and reverses the sequence from the [original] sequence.
The cremation ground is the cause for the assembly circle (*cakramelāpa*) of the *vīrasiddhas*;
one should perform it according to the path of its mantra, wherein there is a single Vidyā divided into six types.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa:
the lamp, the five jewels, the vessel, and the lotus;
the mudrā is that which has five spokes and a single-syllable navel.
One should perform the five [offerings] at the beginning and the end, joined with the five jewels;
then the hero’s conduct shines forth, for the hero desires the state of a hero through the five heroes of the fivefold sequence in the lineage.
Having understood the lineage (*anvaya*) as fivefold, there is the fivefold Vīrasiddhi;
likewise, there is one Vīramudrā and one Vīramudrāmālinī.
Māyā, which severs worldly existence, should be known as the sixfold Mālinī.
O God, Mālinī resides within the five [groups], illuminated by the syllable *aiṃ*,
through the sequence of six divisions and the reversal of the five pairs.
Having understood the fivefold instruction, which is the root of the conduct of the Krama, through the single characteristic and sixfold divisions of the five jewels as its cause.
Situated in the midst of five groups of five, there are five syllables of five;
independent, the supreme non-existence, the five jewels difficult to discern.
The means for the difficult-to-attain [state] is indeed that which is called Kadamba, located between the two points of emission;
it is the power residing within the instruments of action, and that power is situated between the ears.
O Karṇa, having thus understood the power (śakti) and the mantra, one should practice silence;
situated in the midst of silence, he is silent by means of the designation "Aiṃ.
This is from the Kumārikākhaṇḍa.
The syllable Aiṃ is to be known as the five-jeweled [mantra] of the Five Jewels;
the foundation of the Five Jewels is the brilliantly radiant primordial wisdom of the flood.
"Knowing this, liberation is certain; of this there is no doubt"—this is the command (*ājñā*) in the *Ratnapañcaka*.

Thus, in the primordial descent (*avatāra*), in the sacrifice of Māhamanthānabhairava, in the lineage (*anvaya*) measuring seventy million verses, emerged from the path of Meru, exceeding one hundred thousand quarters, brought down to the first seat (*ādyapīṭha*), on the path of the Seat of Knowledge (*vidyāpīṭha*), in the determination of the Pure Sixfold Group (*vimalaṣaṭka*).
In the *Ājñāpārameśvara*, within the division beginning with the letter *ka*, in the description of the chapter on the stages of the Five Jewels,
this is the bliss named the Arising of the Sequence (*Kramodaya*).
The venerable Vakrā said:
"I shall now describe the sixty-third bliss, the stages (*bhūmikā*) of the sixfold knowledge; listen!"
Of the six principles of the Yoginīs, there are six; likewise, the seventh.
The sixth is the seventh ignorance; the sixth is the seventh family.
Their authority over knowledge, however, is established through the instruction on the peak-syllable (kūṭa).
Consisting of six syllables of color and situated within the city of the moon,
she is Kuleśvarī, born into the lineage of the king who is the lunar orb.
Emerging from that body, they reside in the Kadamba grove at Guhāvāsa;
and staying there, the six goddesses abide in their natural state.
These seven are the family deities of the sevenfold division of the Self;
among them, Hara resides on Mount Meru, the king of the family mountains, as its giver.
In the bliss of Hara, the shadow of Hara has become the six deities;
and the six goddesses of the cave reside within the image of the one whose abode is the cave.
Through the instruction on the six seats (*ṣaḍpīṭha*), the ritual action of making [the deity] possessed of seed-syllables (*sabīja*) is performed;
then the Power (*śakti*), through six divisions, has as its sphere of activity the locus of the seed-syllable.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa: The Brahmins constantly worship [her] in the house at the illustrious Candrapura;
she is the one Yoni, the power of Rudra, the deity named Yākṣiṇī.
She is the leader of the path of mantra; by her, the stages have been presided over, as well as the authority over the entire continuum, especially.
This indeed is the first lineage, the seven mother deities;
they know the six stations of the householder to begin with the Foundation (ādhāra) and ending with the Command (ājñā).
Established on the left path is the ring finger, the deity of the sixth [day];
they too have become possessed of form and are endowed with consciousness within the sense faculties.
They float upon the waters of the sky; of this there is no doubt.
And their charioteer is the Vidyā Kartarī, whose presiding deity is Vāmadeva.
She stands at the southern gate; by means of the bliss of the *bhaga*, she is the Southern [Deity].
The goddesses are formed from the seven syllables of the mantra: *ḍa-ra-la-ka-sa-ha-yā*.
Renowned as the first lineage, it was brought down by the Primordial One who possesses the command;
there are seven mudrās, three caves, and a single abode within the cave.
Thus, in the *Saṃvarta*, the instruction on the secret cave proceeds;
within these mandalas, the sacrifice is performed in six ways for each of the six.
Established by way of the mantra-path, it is the instruction for the "Bursting of the Jar" (*ghaṭasphoṭa*):
"The letter *ḍa*, the single *ambikā*, and the three successive steps of the letter *e*;
having pierced [the target] with the seven *e*s, one should then perform the suppression (*nigraha*)."
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa: the letter *ra* is pierced by radiance, and likewise situated in the middle of Hara’s belly.
And the mere knowledge of the designation "kha" [is established] within the self through the sequence of six divisions;
the syllable *la*, situated in the middle of the mobile, is the triad of *la* divided fivefold.
The knowledge of *niyoga* resides in a single *la*-letter; it is the *svādhikārikā*, and the *kakārā* at the end of the *kakārā* is encapsulated within the two *ka*-letters.
Ākīnī, whose nature is like a crow, resides in the center of *ka*;
Śākinī, residing in the center of *śa*, is adorned within the belly of the letter *śa*.
By the power of minor karma, there is the Śākini ending in the letter Śa;
Hākinī resides in the middle of the swan within the fourfold group of swans.
Hākinī is the disintegration of separation from the midst of the sky;
Yākinī resides in the midst of birth, having pierced through the six families.
The Supreme Goddess Yākinī is the subduer of the channel of waves;
she resides in the Kumārikā-khaṇḍa by means of the division of the forty-nine [deities] through the command of the forty-nine cities.
There are seven peaks in sequence; the eighth step consists of seven, seven, and eight syllables.
And the name of the eighth step consists of eight syllables.
They are perfected even from separation, even from the ocean by means of the seven;
the vowels are produced by the seven, and the Rudras by the seven-times-seven.
By means of the seven, there is the convention of the flood; it is the lineage succession of the seven times seven.
It is the sevenfold arising, the sevenfold illumination, by way of the designation of the seventh vowel.
The heart of the seven goddesses is the heart joined with the five;
the heart is divided sevenfold, as is the family divided sevenfold.
The seal of Akula, known as Abhinnā, is Kāpālinī;
she is the skull of the seventh, and the seventh of the skull.
The seventh command is Śiva Ananta; the skull has become sevenfold.
Of the letter *ḍa* and the skull, the deity is named Karkaṭī.
By means of separation, the powerful [mantra] is the skull (kapāla) divided by the letters beginning with *ḍa*;
it consists of the letters beginning with *ḍa*, situated in the middle of those beginning with *ḍa*, together with five instances of the letter *u*.
Through the awakening to the five superknowledges, the letter *ḍa* is the name of the rākṣasī of six kinds.
In the Great Conjunction (mahāmelāpaka) battle, Hāṭakī belongs to Rakapāla; [there is] Rakapāla, three times Rak.
— *Kumārikākhaṇḍa*
The three syllables *ra*, *ka*, and *ra* are for the sun, the jewel, and the skull-cup.
The syllable *ka* of the skull-bearer Vikapālaka is the word for "skull";
the syllable *la* of the skull is the yakṣiṇī named Lampaṭā.
By the word "his inner apartments" (tasyāntapura), there are two *la*s and three [syllables];
[the sequence is] *valā*, *mekala*, *lakemobhau*, and *lalīlākapālakam*.
The skull-bowl of Karālāmalaka consists of one hundred thousand syllables;
it is the supreme syllable, the secret named Karparī belonging to the letter *ka* and the skull-bowl.
And in the wheel of the conduct of the pledge (samayācāracakra), she has assumed the form of a crow;
she is the letter *ka*, the form of a crow, the letter *ka*, and the skull-bowl (*karpara*) resting upon the letter *ka*.
Kālī is [the consort] of Kaṅkālakāla; Kapālāmṛtabhairava is [the consort] of Śakāra; and Śavarī, born from the womb of a Daitya, is [the consort] of Kapāla.
In battle, having drunk blood, there is mud and a skull;
again, in battle, there is mud with three *sakāras* and a *repha*.
The letter *ra* is without *repha*, and the skull is situated upon the letter *kha*;
the deity of the skull of the letter *ha* is Haṭadūtī.

Through the application of the night-walker’s practice, when the two skull-bowls are in the state of the letter *ha*, she is Haṭanī; that is the fivefold knowledge of the letter *ha* of the skull-bowl.
The skull known as Haṭṭa belongs to the syllable *hakāra*;
it is the Kumārikākhaṇḍa.
The syllable of the skull of *yakāra* is the form of Virajā.
And that skull, known as the trident, consists of six parts;
it is the "trident" (triśūla) because of the sequence of the three prongs (tri-śūla) and the two prongs (śūla).
Having pierced the city in the midst of the dust with the trident and the skull-cup,
the seven goddesses [enter] the skull-cup; the skull-cup is divided into seven parts,
and that one [goddess], through sevenfold divisions, is established as seven by means of those seven.
By means of the sevenfold probe of knowledge, one swallows the seven-times-seven portions.
Having understood the seven-times-seven instruction, which consists of the seven families,
the tradition of the seven-syllable family situated within the tradition of the ocean.
The Piṇḍāmnāya is the essence of all [mantras]; the seven deities of the sacred seats (pīṭhas);
and among the deities, the immutable ones residing within the seed-syllables beginning with the Praṇava.
Knowledge alone is the differentiating power, the all-devouring, most wonderful;
it is the devouring situated within the act of devouring, the peak of devouring in its manifold forms.
That one [power] is divided into seven; she is fond of devouring, the supreme command of the instruments, the pervasion of pervasion, and the vision and action of the instruments.
In the state of being the agent of the knowledge of the instruments,
the instrument is the suppression of impurity;
in the state of oneness with the stainlessness of the Guhas, there is the deity of the Guha.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa,
through the illumination of the secret cave, there is the unique cave of the Supreme Goddess;
for by her command, the bliss of the cave, the bliss of the creative power (kalā), and the flood of bliss [arise].
Consciousness is immortal time; through the seven arts of consciousness, there are seven goddesses, seven arts, seven houses, and seven spokes.
By the blossoming of their awakening, there is expansion at the seventh step.
Expansion is sevenfold; the rays of the expansion and the tasting [of bliss] are eight, for they are the digits of the flood of rays. One is the supreme digit.
This is the ocean of the knowledge of conceptualization and the knowledge that transcends conceptualization.
The command of Śiva resides in the center of Śiva; it is the ground of the realization of Śiva.
That Śiva, whose nature consists of the threads and digits of Śiva, is the thirty-six deities;
he is the power residing within the ocean, the Great Power known as the sixfold one.
Six times six is thirty-six; six times five is thirty; six times fivefold is the digit (kalā).
The six oceans, the six measures, the instruction on the six measures,
the six, the thirty-six divisions, and the mudrās divided into thirty-six.
The reality of pervasion consists of six aspects and causes the blossoming of the sixfold consciousness;
the mudrā situated within the jar is likewise sevenfold.
The single mudrā, which is the pervasion of the three types of syllables, should pervade the world;
it is the Vidyā that effects the pervasion of the world, illuminated by the sixteen vowels.
If power resides in consciousness by will, that distinction of power arises from threefold division;
that threefold power, illuminated by the imperishable one who possesses the three qualities, exists within the three.
The three states are also in expansion; [therein is] Vikāsānandabhairavī.
Those heroes who arise from the wheel of the Mothers by way of the path of the heroes—[this is] the Kumārikākhaṇḍa.
The Island-Seal (dvīpamudrā) is established as the island; it is the first family (kula) of the group of six.
It consists of the lineage of the families (kulakrama), the Vidyā, and the succession of the three lineages of the families.
In the tradition (āmnāya), Bhairavānanda resides within the wheel (cakra), situated in the midst of the Mothers.
Among the Mothers, the middle Mother is Mātṛvidyā and Khiḍḍiṇī.
The *khinkhinī* is sixfold through its divisions; this is the mudrā that assumes forms at will.
It is the pinnacle of delight for the Mothers of the Mother-circle and for the circle itself.
And at the edge of Śekhara is Kailāsa; on Kailāsa is the circle of the Mothers, and the assembly of the Mothers occurs at the Udyāna seat.
Remaining there, one should desire the seven Mothers, who are to be differentiated from the Goddess;
and for all the Mothers, [one should perform the rite] with the eight-pronged pin of the Yoginīs.
The power that causes division within the maṇḍala is Śakti, and she is the Kaulikī Vidyā.
Kaulikī resides in the center of Kula and is the one who expands the knowledge of Kaula.
That latent predisposition of others arises through the differentiation of impelling forces;
at the end of the predisposition, it becomes the illusion of the mind, which is encapsulated by the end of that illusion.

Through the mode of becoming one at the end of latent impressions (*vāsanā*), there is the state of *manonmanā*. This mode has been fully explained according to its sixfold nature. Thus, the Self is indeed sixfold, having the three qualities (*guṇa*) brought to cessation. *Kumārikākhaṇḍa* [ends]. Then the power of cessation, the Mother Dakārāmbā, is established.
Constantly abiding like a bell, consisting of the movement of day and night,
that power known as Ghaṇṭālakā is proclaimed to begin with the letter *ra*.
In the unity of rising and setting, she is the letter Śa and she is Śāṅkarī;
then the power consisting of six sheaths is established as the letter La and the others.
She is the power that differentiates the two supreme joys through the distinction of going and coming; at that time, she is the differentiating power established in the letters beginning with *ka*,
established in the letters beginning with *ka*.
She who brings about awakening through the six mudrās has a body consisting of the sixfold bliss;
she is then the blissful maiden (Kumārī) who discerns the letters beginning with 'A'.
Between the anus and the penis is the *prāṇa*; at the end of the *prāṇa* is the arising of Bhairava.
Then there is that which is called the "Opening," which pervades the letters beginning with *ha*.
(Kumārikākhaṇḍa)
When the mind at the end of the pervasive [state] and that which is illusion become threefold,
then she is Raudrī, consisting of the three qualities and established in the letters beginning with *ya*.
In the center of the *bhaga* is the power (*śakti*) of the *bhaga*; in the center of the *bhaga* is the form of the *bhaga*.
The power born from the bliss of the *bhaga* pervades the entire body of the *bhaga*.
The state of pervasion is the pervasion of the *kalās*; it occurs in three ways in the void (*kha*).
It is also threefold and fivefold on the path; then there is that which expands the path:
the path of the six-cornered world and the path of the six-cornered sphere.

In the midst of the monastery is she known as Ḍā, the goddess Ḍāmā, the Kṣetrapārvatī who dwells within the interior of the mountain; she is the shatterer of the mountain-peaks and the crossroads of the paths,
having divided her own self into the womb and causing agitation of the mind.
In the state of being the agent who effects the cause of the lion, there are two lions within the agency;
these two pairs, divided according to their form, are embodied in the letter *la*.
When the Self is at the end of the letter *la*, it is abandoned as a state beyond negation;
that power which has arisen as bliss is the letter *sa*, the crest-jewel of the mountain. —From the *Kumārikākhaṇḍa*.
Between the two peaks of the stone, there is indeed a widow (raṇḍā) facing downwards;
by reversing the letter *siṃhaka*, it is known as the letter *sa* with the name "Lion" (*siṃha*).
The power that resides within the womb of the lotus is Haṃsinī, the deity of yoga;
she is the syllable *Ha*, the command-syllable of the ripening of the self of yoga.
The power contained within the letter *ya* is the *bhaga* (vulva) in the center of the belly of the *haṃsa*;
the letter *ya* is the self abiding on Mount Meru, the Blessed Lord Śiva.
Thus, the power whose nature is moisture has proceeded fivefold for the sake of emanation;
the goddess Raudrī likewise becomes one who knows the distinction between going and coming.
That which is the fierce Māyā is Vāmā;
she is Suṣumṇā, and she is remembered as Jyeṣṭhā, the shatterer of the abode of Jyeṣṭhā.
The one called Bhañjanī is proclaimed as established within the Bhagavān;
because she is dissolved in the midst of the *rajas*, she is the power of *rajas* that brings about downfall.
Furthermore, the arising of that downfall is accomplished through the supreme Vidyā.
The six deities reside upon the petals of a six-spoked lotus; they occupy the six petals.
The leaf that is beyond the end of the measure—that leaf is the mouth of Vāḍava;
when [that] is attained, it is known as Tuṣṭi-yoga, and the yogin remembers Bhairava.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa,
that form of Bhairava’s sacred seat which is Vīravikrama stands as the stainless, sinless Hero, established through the application of the conduct of heroes (vīracaryā).
And that Power (śakti) is designated by the name of the letter Ū; she is the Kaulikī arising in the letter E.
She should be known as the Middle (madhyamā), the Action (kriyā) whose essence consists of the phonemes E and Ū.
The letter *e* and the two *ū*s moving upwards are the *repha* (the letter *r*) encapsulated within the neuter (*na-puṃsaka*);
the letter *ū* is situated between the supreme (*para*) and the middle (*madhya*).
Power is sevenfold.
One should apply the yoga in seven ways, for the form of the seven worlds is both form and transformation; when those seven are realized, that is the state of the Sky-farer (Khecara).

Having understood that the center of space belongs to the Lord of Birds (Garuḍa), that the maṇḍala resides within the Lord of Birds, and that his station is the "enveloped" (saṃpuṭa) state, one indeed attains the eternal plane.
Wherever the letter *ya* of the cessation of mental fluctuations (*cittavṛttinirodha*) abides, by the power of the pierced energy (*viddha-śakti*), that energy becomes straight.
And then there arises the state [of attainment], which is fivefold: trembling, possession, shaking, moving, and pervading the feet.
The arising of conditions through states occurs in five ways;
when there is impulsion at the letter *ya*, then the Kaulika [principle] is agitated.
Kaulīśa is known as Bindu and Nāda; [he resides] in Nāda, Bindu, and Visarga.
His Śakti-bīja, moreover, becomes threefold as Bīja and Śakti.

O God, he who perceives the letter *ṭha* in three ways as being without remainder, because all parts have dissolved away, then attains the state of the *Haṃsa*. In the womb of the *Haṃsa* of the world, O Kumārikā, resides the first digit (*kalā*).
And she is Caṇḍāmā, also known as Umā, the illuminator of awakening;
she is the deity of the Kaula at the time of its arising within the six [traditions].
And that deity in the Guhāmnāya is likewise of six types.
Thus, in the introduction to the Great Sacrifice of Manthānabhairava, in the lineage comprising seventy million verses emerged from the Path of Meru,
exceeding one hundred thousand quarters, on the path of the Seat of Knowledge (vidyāpīṭha), in the determination of the Sixfold Subsequent Pure Division,
in the *Kādi* division, in the *Svāminīmata*, the supreme command of the Lord, accompanied by the venerable twenty-four thousand [verses].
In the discourse spoken by the Mother, in the description of the stages of the sixfold command,
this is the bliss named the Arising of the Sequence (Kramodaya).
The venerable Vakrā said:
Now is sung the tradition of the stages (bhūmikā) suitable for the fivefold and threefold [teachings], which are entirely stainless.
The sixty-fourth bliss is the repose of Vimalā, which has overcome the abode of the senses;
the stainless self, the Vimalā-abode, is remembered as fivefold.
And their stainless power is the division known as "Stainless" (vimala);
through the division of the "Stainless Designation" (saṃjñāvimalabheda), there is the Stainless Mandala sequence.
The mandala named Vimala is designated by the name of the Vimala tree;
at that time, she possesses a stainless form through five distinct modes.
The stainless one is divided fivefold, and power (śakti) likewise is divided fivefold;
the Supreme Self (paramātman) is divided into two types within the ritual procedure of the Bhagas.
For those who are beginningless and endless, by the beginningless and stainless command,
the fivefold Vimala has been proclaimed through the division of the five commands.
The self that is stainless and free from conceptualization, the omniscient one who bears the moon upon his crest;
the crest-jewel of all, the self through every form of consciousness.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa:
He who knows the dissolution of all things, who illumines the rays of gnosis,
who is light, stainless bliss, the Single Foot, and whose banner is the crest-fire.

The spear has the banner of Śikhidhvaja; nectar is the banner of Ahicchatra. Situated in the midst of the banner and the flag is the immortal self of all beings. In the middle of the banner is the spear-banner, and that is Raudrī, the Manonmanā.
Unmanā has five divisions, and she is known by the name Sarvajñā.
Śikhin is the light of the digit of the moon; that light is the crest-ornament of the peak. At the crest, Śekharānanda is the peak that has become fivefold.
On the peak there is a fivefold pervasion; the abode of the peak of the sacrifice is the abode in the form of Malaya, consisting of the fivefold nature of Malaya.
The teaching of Śiva is the manifestation of the object experienced by the fivefold self;
it is a teaching that is abundant, infinite, undivided, imperishable, and free from defects.
Cessation is the bliss of delight, ever fearless and auspicious;
it is the teaching through the abandonment of piercing, awakened, and characterized by the sense organs.
Ātmānava was the son of Śṛṅga; his son was Ārāma; Ārāma’s son was Kalpasāgara;
Sāgara’s son was Manaḥ; and Manaḥ’s son was Setubandha, the builder of the bridge of Setu.
Through the application of the three groups of five, for both conjunction and dissolution,
that which consists of the essence of the bliss of emanation then becomes the pentad.
In the *Kumārikākhaṇḍa*, within the three horns of the bound soul (*paśu*), there is the *lakṣa*, the *alakṣa*, the *viraja*, the *rajas*,
the nourishment of all things, the stainless, and the five-night rite (*pañcarātrika*).
The cage of the stainless Pañcarātra is the Pañcarātrika;
it is the sky of three nights and four quarters, and one who is enveloped by that is truly born.
Residing within the body of the knowledge of one’s own mantra, by means of the designation "the row of tongues" (rasanāvalī),
the power that is thus most firmly bound is difficult to discern due to the strength of the three folds (trivalī).
She is the single source of all beings and of mantras of immeasurable power, who is the desire within the family, known by the various designations of the stainless divisions.
The peaks are five, the digits are five, and indeed the seed-syllables are five;
through the metaphorical application of their conjunction, this pentad is known as "beginningless."
The true essence of mantra, which makes one's side firm, should be understood as "pañca-pañcaka-pañcānāṃ pañca-pañca-kalāv ubhau."
The Support (Ādhāra) is extracted from the abode of all embodied beings of every caste;
it is extracted through the division of the sixfold knowledge into five groups of five.
It is the God who is both the indivisible divider and the divider of the two powers of differentiation and non-differentiation.
Supreme bliss, the bliss of action, and bliss—these have arisen in five ways.
The lower consists of the letters from *na* to *pha*, and the intermediate consists of four quarters;
when the three quarters are unified as one, the Tree of Quarters (*padavṛkṣa*) is composed of the three [levels].
Silent, it is adorned with the peak of the expansion of the space of the single syllable;
the stainless power residing therein is known as that which causes agitation in the insentient.
Kumārikākhaṇḍa:
Thus, silence is the supreme mass, the mass that is the single-syllable syllable.
The bird situated in the middle of its wings is the triad of *ha*, the mandala of silence.
Thus, in brief, is the enumeration of the three *hakāras* and the five [syllables],
according to the divisions of six, seven, eight, nine, and eighteen.
Where there is a reversal of action from one reversed word to another word—
where words are the five syllables of a word, and a word is a single syllable.
The single syllable is the individual soul (jīva), joined with the digit of emission (visarga);
it is the unconquered supreme seed-syllable, the last of the five primordial ones.
Free from the first five, adorned with the middle five,
and abiding in the five of the final five— this is the word of twenty-five syllables.
The practice of the five stages of the path consists of the left-hand practice and the right-hand practice;
the right-hand practice is the western practice, and the western practice is the dissolution of all things.
Then, due to its oneness with the abode of dissolution, the state is said to be difficult to discern;
everything is fivefold, and the final [state] has proceeded in five ways.
Indeed, the fivefold mass is fivefold; it has gone to the right in five ways.
The former mass is fivefold, and the small mass is fourfold.
Thus has been described the path, the fourfold path of accomplishment, through the fourfold expansion of gnosis: the Kaulika [path] consisting of the bliss of intrinsic nature.
The Kumārikākhaṇḍa: the bliss of the Kula and Kaula, the Kulamātaṅgabhairava,
the ocean of all beings, and the pervasive Great Garden.
Situated there, the tree itself is divided into five branches;
through the application of *nāda* and *bindu*, the pentad of powers (*śakti-pañcaka*) has arisen.
“First, the knowledge of the lineage (anvaya-jñāna) proceeds through five modes of cognition;
once it is known to abide in these five ways, ignorance is instantly eliminated.”
In the center of the beginningless mountain, amidst the trees, is the Kadamba grove;
the cave is Kadambinī, where liberation—the deity—has become fivefold.
Immaculate and pure from the beginningless past, she is designated by the syllable *E*;
having crossed over the mountain range of the Himavat, she has become the *Śṛṅgāṭā*.
The Omniscient One, situated in the midst of the mountain, is the one who shatters the syllables *u* and *ū*;
O God, in the convention of the tortoise, she is born as the nature of the net.
Āmūlā and Yogadevī, whose seat is the support of another's body,
are the stainless Yogadevatā because of their dissolution into the supreme fullness.
In the space of the letters of the Siddhaliṅga is Śṛṅgāṭākṣarabhairavī;
Śavarī is the Brahma-knot of the Siddhaliṅgas in the supreme state.

In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa: In the state of tranquility there is supreme bliss (*parānanda*), and in its blossoming is the station of Ciñciṇī. The goddess Campakā arises from the syllable *oṃ* for the sake of accomplishment.
In the sequence of the five fields, through the purification of the five seats, the Goddess [attains] the Pure Pentad by means of the mind of Śivānanda.
The *sarvasthā* is the *kiṅkiṇī* mudrā; it becomes the syllable of the *karavīra*.
Through various forms and colors, the triad is designated by the single syllable *e*.
The head of *kha* is the letter *kha*, and the head of *ha* is the letter *ha*;
the head of *ra* is the letter *ha*, and the head of *ja* is the letter *ja*.
Having first understood the pervasive bliss of the head, the fivefold pentad of conventions,
and the [other] pentad, one becomes stainless in an instant.
The single *śilā* is that of desire-form; the auspicious *śilā* consists of five syllables.
The syllables are the five *padas*, and the *padas* are joined with the five *śilās*.
In the birth [of the syllable], the stone that stands in the midst of the birth is the piercing Śakti;
she is the radiance who effects the single wheel, that stone possessing the splendor of Brahman.
Then the birth-origination occurred within the syllable of the *janma-śṛṅgāṭaka*.
But the stone of the western seat shall be the birth-stone.
O Bhava, when the exhaustion of seven births is reached, that stone is obtained,
wherein the fivefold power resides in bliss within the circle of the Mothers.
She is the knowledge and the object of knowledge of the entire treasury of mantras;
she is declared to be that first stone, this deity who is a Yoginī.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa: The single Birth-Brahma-stone, endowed with six trees,
produces the five states after the act of churning has been performed.
One may obtain the creeper of Mahendra, Harendra, and Khagendra;
that indeed is the threefold means, which further becomes a triad of divisions.
The entire web of the digits of consciousness is the mandala of the sixteen vowels;
and the three phonemes situated therein constitute the definitive teaching of the Trika.
The letter *a* in the middle, the letter *ā*, the letter *i*, and the day of the qualities (*guṇavāsara*)—
by means of this application within the self of passion (*suratātman*), one attains the letter *a*, the supreme ocean.
The letter *ī*, the letter *u*, and the letter *sa*—these three are the rays;
the placement of the middle word is within the sphere of the power (*śakti*) of the letter *sa*.
The syllable *ku* in the middle and the syllable *ū*, which is the threefold *vāgbhava*;
that is the unmanifest, the supreme *liṅga*, headless, and the sphere of all-pervasion.
The wheel divided by the thirty-three [deities], that wheel is the determination of the *bindu*;
it is joined with the full *kalā*, the triple-triad of the mass of heroes (*vīrarāśi*).
The three syllables of Trikaṇṭaka are *trikaṇṭā-kaṇṭakāni*;
and *kaṭara*, *rakaṭāṭa*, and *ṭharayu* constitute Trikaṇṭaka.
That which is called the secret convention of the three has been extracted even from the ocean;
having been extracted by way of the left path, it makes [the mantra] become triple-guṇa.

In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa, the letter *e* belongs to the letter *ca*; the second [syllable] is at the end of the letter *e*. When bliss is joined with two long vowels, then success (*siddhi*) occurs in the triad.
When even that which is one becomes threefold, such that the triad of qualities constitutes a single family, then that is the form of Bhairavī, arising even from the non-dual flow.
And he is the non-dual Lord of the Stone, the manifest Ḍāmarabhairava;
he is the seed of all living beings, for the body is indeed one and infinite.
The infinite, motionless seed of the partless consciousness and cognition;
you are the indivisible, pervasive Lion-form, both transcendent and immanent.
The flow of the flood of bliss belonging to the seed that is both transcendent and immanent, stainless and luminous— that is the Youthful (Kumāra), who is both transcendent and immanent.
The desire for another and the desire for oneself is the seed of the higher and lower;
having entered existence through these three, the yogi experiences the "three thorns."
Furthermore, O Lord of Śilā, that which was called the state of Brahman is situated within primordial nature (prakṛti) yet remains extremely remote,
just as one might draw water using a lotus-stalk fiber.
The syllable of Brahman in its entirety.
The deity Viṣṇu of the Lākula [tradition] has the form of a shimmering flash of lightning.
Vahni is situated in the center as Viṣṇu, known as the seed-syllable, the sun of the sky;
Sūkṣma is situated in the center of Bhānu, and then Rudra is the sky-clad one.
Through the abandonment of ostentation, he stands in the middle within the threefold self.
The Trikāyayoga: the Western practice of Kramācāra by way of the left-hand form.
The left [channel] is on the left, and the end of the left is enclosed within the interior of the left;
having clearly understood these two cavities, the path of the knowable arises.
The seed-syllable of the Lord of the Family of Prajāpati is the fiery sphere (vahnigolaka);
within that sphere, the syllable of sound is the letter *sa*, which is by nature quiescent.
In the Kumārikākhaṇḍa:
Having made the mind one-pointed, the intellect becomes steady and dissolved;
then, for those of noble lineage, there arises the Kaulika knowledge of the Kula, which is like an ocean.
The immortal one, the lord of the fly-whisks, from the world of immortal knowledge,
is the light of all beings— the single reality that has come forth in three ways.
The triple-triangle is indeed the one perfected in three kalās; the power of the Siddhas becomes threefold.
